transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Asha, Samir, Lina (Nyx)

Summary (auto):
Quick scoping for a 6-week pilot focused on inference unit economics and latency SLAs for a staging environment. Discussed expected throughput, average prompt sizes, caching/batching knobs, and the bench plan. Agreed next steps: send cost model, share bench script, schedule bench run.

---

[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, thanks for making time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Asha: Asha here. Samir here. Lina here.
[00:09] Diego: Diego from Redwood, SE. I'll be running the bench with you.
[00:12] Maya: Great. high level objective — figure out whether Redwood Dedicated pilot fits Nyx's budget and latency needs in staging, and define bench scope and success criteria.

[00:28] Samir: To ground this — we want to run a customer-facing assist feature in staging that mimics production: ~1k concurrent users at peak, average prompt ~1.8k tokens, responses ~600 tokens. Our target is p95 latency <200ms and overall cost below our runway threshold.

[00:46] Diego: OK, that's helpful. quick clarifying Qs: what models are you currently evaluating internally?
[00:51] Samir: We're trialing OpenAI for dev and Lambda Labs on prem for some workloads. We also have a small in-house llama-ish model for retrieval.

[01:02] Maya: Perfect. so for the pilot we usually do two bench axes: unit economics (per-token) and latency at load. we'll propose a bench with: synthetic traffic to match your qps, two model variants (a quantized 13B and a FP16 33B), and cache on/off passes.

[01:29] Asha: Quick sanity check — pricing ballpark. Our finance wants a per-1k-token estimate for hosted vs dedicated, and a best-case with batching/caching.

[01:40] Maya: Right. rough numbers to start — hosted typical is around $0.004 to $0.008 per 1k tokens depending on model; Dedicated can drop that materially, to something like $0.0008 to $0.002 per 1k tokens when you combine reserved GPU amortization plus efficient batching. but those are naive numbers — bench will give actual.

[02:05] Lina: Wait that's an order of magnitude difference, can you break down where the savings come from?

[02:09] Diego: Sure. there are three levers: 1) reserved capacity amortizes GPU infra, 2) batching increases tokens/sec throughput so per-token GPU time goes down, 3) caching (prefix/KV) means not all tokens are computed every time — for reuse patterns this can cut token compute by 30-70%. also quantized kernels reduce GPU memory and improve throughput.

[02:41] Samir: On caching — our assist re-uses user context often, maybe 40% prefix reuse. how do you simulate that in a bench?

[02:48] Diego: We parameterize bench scripts: prefix reuse rate, prompt length distribution, and qps ramp. We'll run multiple passes: cold-cache, warm-cache with 40% reuse, and aggressive reuse scenario. that lets us estimate effective tokens generated and token compute saved.

[03:10] Asha: Success criteria from Nyx side: 1) p95 latency under 200ms for interactive flows, 2) pilot unit cost <= $0.002 per 1k tokens averaged over benched workload, 3) integration with our VPC and audit logs for compliance. If any of these fail we won't move to full roll out.

[03:31] Maya: Noted. we'll map bench outputs to those criteria. one nuance: p95 can be sensitive to batching windows. if your client expects single-digit latency, we may need micro-batch and lower batch sizes which raises per-token cost. there's always a tradeoff.

[03:50] Lina: Our infra team wants to avoid major network changes. what's typical for VPC/private deployment?

[03:56] Diego: For Redwood Private/Dedicated we do VPC peering or private link. Lina, we can send an architecture note but typical latency hit for peering is minimal; biggest impact is NAT egress rules and any deep packet inspection.

[04:12] Asha: Also SOC2/ISO — we need to see audit docs before pilot approval.

[04:16] Maya: We'll share SOC2 docs and an example AUP.

[04:20] Samir: Back to cost math — can you walk through a toy calc for our numbers? assume 1k concurrent users, average prompt 1.8k tokens, response 600 tokens, 40% prefix reuse.

[04:31] Diego: Sure. naive tokens generated per interaction ~2400, but with 40% reuse effective new tokens computed = 2400 * (1 - 0.4) = 1440. if your qps at peak is 1k concurrent assuming 0.5 rps per user that's 500 rps, so 500 * 1440 = 720k tokens/sec? that's too high — hold on, math correction. 500 rps * 1440 tokens = 720k tokens per second; over an hour that's huge. probably you meant 1k concurrent with 0.05 rps? clarify expected RPS.

[05:05] Samir: Sorry, yes — peak qps ~120 RPS. our concurrency estimate was off.

[05:10] Diego: OK with 120 RPS * 1440 = 172,800 tokens/sec, which is 622M tokens/hour. that times hosted per-token rate gets big, so Dedicated is usually the only practical option at that scale. again bench will produce real GPU utilization numbers.

[05:33] Maya: To sanity-check cost, if Dedicated gives you $0.001 per 1k tokens, 622M tokens/hour => 622k thousands tokens => $622/hour — multiply that by avg hours used per day. But this example shows we need more precise traffic numbers and usage windows.

[05:55] Asha: Our estimated daily active usage is 3 hours of peak per day — so we'd want monthly chewable numbers.

[06:03] Diego: Yes we'll provide monthly extrapolation in the spreadsheet. Also, batching magic: if we can batch 8 requests per GPU step we can reduce GPU time per token. but high batch sizes increase tail latency.

[06:20] Samir: What's your recommended batch size for p95 <200ms?

[06:24] Diego: For a 13B quantized model on a A100-like worker, single-digit batch sizes (2-4) usually keep p95 low; for 33B you may need 1-2 to hit p95 targets. Quantized 13B often gives better cost/latency sweet spot. We'll bench both.

[06:45] Maya: We'll include a recommended config table: model, expected tokens/sec, recommended batch window, estimated per-1k cost under warm-cache and cold-cache.

[06:58] Asha: Bench timeline? we need results before our August 21st steering review.

[07:02] Diego: Proposed schedule: this week - collect logs + confirm traffic patterns; next week - Diego runs bench with Redwood infra (2 runs: warm/cold); week after - analyze and share cost model + config recommendations. so 10 days-ish. is that workable?

[07:22] Asha: Yes. we'll aim to turn around sample logs in 48 hours.

[07:26] Lina: On the bench machines — can you match our staging GPU types? we're running on NVidia T4 / some p4s.

[07:32] Diego: We can mimic hardware families. bench will report on the specific instance types and we can map to your T4s. some perf will differ vs A100 class. we'll call that out in the report.

[07:45] Samir: Any concerns about tokenization differences across models? we saw different token counts between the model we used and other vendors.

[07:52] Diego: Yes tokenizer mismatch affects token counts — bench will normalize by running your real prompts against each model to capture actual tokenization. please include raw inputs.

[08:05] Maya: Security question: retention and logging — can we limit logs to metadata and exclude PII?

[08:10] Diego: Absolutely. Redwood's default for Dedicated pilot can be configured to redact or not persist payloads, and we support customer-managed KMS for keys. we'll provide the options doc.

[08:24] Asha: Great. Also, are there quick wins on cost with compilation/quantization?

[08:29] Diego: In many cases quantized kernels reduce memory bandwidth and allow more concurrency, reducing per-token time by 20-40%. Combined with prefix caching for your reuse patterns, you might see effective cost drops ~30-60% versus raw host calls. but we need bench to quantify.

[08:49] Samir: For the bench run itself — what telemetry will you capture?

[08:52] Diego: We'll capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, batch size distribution, cache hit rates, and request-level traces for any tail events. we'll send a CSV and a short dashboard.

[09:07] Lina: Are we able to run a test with VPC peering so network characteristics are similar?

[09:12] Diego: Yes — we can run the bench from a peered VPC or from Redwood's staging in the same cloud region. for this pilot, it's best if you provide a staging VPC we can peer to for at least the bench timeframe.

[09:26] Maya: Ok quick recap on deliverables: 1) Maya — pilot pricing + cost model spreadsheet, 2) Diego — bench script and schedule, 3) Nyx — sample prompts, tokenized counts, and VPC contact, 4) Redwood — SOC2 docs. all due early next week.

[09:46] Asha: sounds good. small ask — can you give an example line item of what a monthly Dedicated bill looks like for a small pool?

[09:53] Maya: Example: a small Dedicated pool (2x A100 equivalent nodes) with reserved capacity might run $xk/month plus per-token/effective usage true-ups. we'll convert to concrete numbers in the spreadsheet.

[10:07] Samir: Let's talk risk scenarios — if warm cache doesn't hit expected reuse, cost balloons. any mitigation?

[10:12] Diego: We build fallback policies — route low latency critical requests to smaller models or replicate prefix cache at the edge to increase hit rate. we can also tune client-side to pin longer-lived contexts for reuse.

[10:26] Asha: Integration question — do you support function/tool calling and structured outputs? our pipeline expects JSON tools.

[10:32] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports function calling and structured output. Diego will include sample payloads and how that affects token counts.

[10:40] Samir: On day-to-day ops — will we get cost breakdown by route/model?

[10:44] Diego: Yes, the Console gives token-level cost per model/route, per-api-key breakdown, and traces. we'll show a demo if helpful in the next call.

[10:56] Lina: One more — latency SLA during autoscaling/backoff. what happens if throughput spikes?

[11:00] Diego: We config autoscaler and fallback policies — graceful degradation includes model fallback (-> smaller model) and region fallbacks. for pilot, you'll specify acceptable fallbacks or prefer request queueing vs failing.

[11:18] Maya: Any other questions?
[11:20] Asha: No, I think we're aligned. please send the materials.

[11:24] Maya: We'll target sending spreadsheets and bench script tomorrow. Diego will ping to schedule exact bench window.

[11:29] Samir: Perfect. thanks all.
[11:30] Maya: Thanks everyone.
